experiments.title: L1 curriculum · TRL + Muon · eight rollouts
experiments.intent: Train the pinned Laguna policy through TRL across all 50 unchanged L1 tasks in easy-first order, using eight trajectories per task and exact root-only credit.
experiments.change: Checkpoint-correct rotary settings; constructor-aware CUDA verification; eight trajectories at initial concurrency four; 1,024-token recovery; phase-shared inference and training on the existing two L40S GPUs.
experiments.conclusion: Snapshot 19 October, 09:48 UTC: four tasks have saved optimizer updates (subtraction, sigmoid, softplus, hardswish). The driver is alive with policy version 4 and has moved to task 0018. This is pipeline progress, not evidence of improved held-out quality. The downloaded attempt view can lag this live state.
experiments.decision: Continue automatic generation, sequential final verification, probability audit, Muon update and checkpoint phases. The user authorized $60 total from the original cost baseline; the live process still caches its original $40 guard until a safe resume. No morning stop. Check hourly; do not interrupt a healthy job to reload the guard.
limitations: This is a saved status snapshot, not a live process monitor. Trackio reports live phase metrics.
Only four of 50 tasks have confirmed saved updates at this snapshot. Step-4 local backup and checksum verification are pending the next artifact sync.
Trackio uses separate generation, scoring and one-update trainer runs. A single continuous optimizer-loss curve is not yet wired.
Reference KL is not computed because beta is zero; missing KL must not be interpreted as zero divergence.
Dollar costs use the displayed rate, not an invoice. The VM continues billing when GPU processes stop.
The registry was refreshed after launch; it is not a new attestation of the immutable source snapshot.

experiments.title: Train exact RLM turns with TRL on two L40S
experiments.intent: Can fast tensor-parallel inference supply genuine CUDA RLM trajectories for a correctly normalized native TRL/Muon update on the same GPU pair?
experiments.change: Separate vLLM runtime; exact per-turn prompts and root-only targets; trajectory-level GRPO advantages; native DAPO PPO loss; phase-separated one-step training and compact adapter export.
experiments.conclusion: A real L1 group produced 22 exact root turns and one native TRL/Muon update. Compact export, CPU read-back and vLLM trained-adapter inference passed. Rewards were 0.1/0/0.1/0.1; zero of four kernels were correct. The update carried submission-format signal, not positive correctness/speed signal.
experiments.decision: Keep the TRL/TP2 training route. Fix constructor-state interfaces and verifier feedback delays, then audit sampler/learner clipping before spending on a longer run.
limitations: No quality improvement is established by one update or by adapter reload.
This run starts from the pinned base, not the old Prime checkpoint.
Full fresh-process optimizer/scheduler/sampler resume remains untested.
Native initial clipping statistic was about 0.306, averaged over microbatches and including padding in metrics.

experiments.title: Resume GRPO and save compact state
experiments.intent: Restore step 1, complete one additional Muon update, and save only adapter and training state without losing resumability.
experiments.change: Preload the pinned base before LoRA restore; exclude frozen base weights from new checkpoints. Keep the old checkpoint unchanged.
experiments.conclusion: Distributed restore from the original full checkpoint and optimizer step 2 passed. The new 68 MB checkpoint passed CPU read-back. This does not establish better kernel generation.
experiments.decision: Validate a distributed restart from the compact checkpoint before a longer run. Keep rank 8 and current hardware limits.
limitations: No distributed restart from the newly compact checkpoint yet.
One admitted cummax group is not a held-out quality comparison.
Recovery turns and child delegation were not exercised.

experiments.title: First saved GRPO update
experiments.intent: Verify the real model can produce rollouts, supply a nonzero GRPO signal, update attention LoRA, and save training state.
experiments.change: Three A100s: one for inference/verifier access and two for expert-parallel training. Rank-8 attention LoRA with Muon.
experiments.conclusion: Step 1 and checkpoint read-back passed. Rewards [0, 0.1, 0, 0.1] supplied submission signal only; no admitted final kernel was correct.
experiments.decision: Use the saved state to validate resume and improve submission reliability before scaling training.
limitations: Three of five saved episodes reached the turn limit.
The original full checkpoint is about 134 GB; preserve it until compact resume is validated.

experiments.title: Give complete CUDA replies more room
experiments.intent: Reduce per-call truncations without expanding the context window or recovery budget.
experiments.change: Normal training reply cap: 2,048 → 4,096. Context remains 12,288; recovery 512; child output 2,048; four rollouts in flight.
experiments.conclusion: 40 focused CPU checks passed. No live model run has tested the larger reply cap.
experiments.decision: Use a bounded validation before a longer training launch; inspect output lengths, context pressure and GPU memory.
limitations: Longer replies may increase latency and context consumption.
No GPU memory or quality result at the new limit.

experiments.title: Make focused delegation easier
experiments.intent: Help the root delegate difficult kernel subproblems without requiring or rewarding unnecessary child calls.
experiments.change: Optional semantics, indexing, algorithm and compiler reviews; a small executable llm_query example stores advice and prints a short slice.
experiments.conclusion: 11 CPU checks passed, including the example through the real worker/proxy with a mocked child. No live delegation benefit is measured.
experiments.decision: Inspect optional child use on harder kernels. Judge correctness, tokens and time, not the number of child calls.
limitations: Children return untested text/code advice; they have no REPL or verifier.
No live comparison for this prompt yet.
